rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Rapid Grant Application: AI Safety Incident Database". It read: "Hi Idris, Thank you for the encouragement at the meetup! I'm submitting an application for the rapid grants round. Please find my two-page proposal attached below. I'm requesting $9,000 to build a comprehensive, searchable database of AI safety incidents over 3 months. Happy to discuss or provide additional information if needed. Best, Morgan --- # Emberfall Fund Rapid Grant Proposal **Applicant**: Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold **Contact**: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org **Amount Requested**: $9,000 **Duration**: 3 months ## Project: AI Safety Incident Database ### What We'll Do We will build a comprehensive, searchable public database of AI safety incidents, failures, near-misses, and concerning behaviors. The database will systematically collect and categorize documented incidents from research papers, news reports, lab disclosures, and community submissions. Each incident will be tagged with standardized metadata: failure type, capability level, consequences, context, and source. We'll deliver: 1. A database of 500+ documented incidents with standardized categorization 2. A public web interface with search, filtering, and data export 3. Methodology documentation for ongoing updates 4. A community submission system 5. Initial trend analysis identifying patterns across incidents **Deliverable timeline**: - Month 1: Foundation (100+ incidents, basic schema and interface) - Month 2: Expansion (300+ incidents, analysis tools, submission system) - Month 3: Launch (500+ incidents, public release on Alignment Commons) ### Why This Project **The gap**: AI safety incidents are scattered across hundreds of sources. There's no comprehensive, searchable database that lets researchers, evaluators, and policymakers see patterns, learn from failures, and understand what kinds of problems are actually occurring as systems become more capable. **Why it matters now**: - The Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule (comment period closes Nov 20) will require labs to report serious incidents, creating new data streams - As AI systems become more capable, learning from past failures becomes increasingly critical - Evidence-based safety work requires systematic data on what actually goes wrong **How it reduces risk**: - Researchers can study failure patterns to develop better safety techniques - Evaluators can design tests based on real-world failure modes - Policymakers can make evidence-based decisions about AI governance - Labs can learn from each other's mistakes without each reinventing the wheel - The community can track whether certain failure types are increasing **What doesn't exist**: While there are scattered incident collections (AI Incident Database focuses on social harms, papers mention specific failures), there's no comprehensive technical safety-focused database with: - Systematic coverage of all documented technical failures - Categorization useful for safety researchers (not just ethics/bias focus) - Regular updates and community contributions - Export tools for analysis ### Why Me (Morgan Hale) **Commitment**: I started Halcyon Threshold because I believe the arrival of superintelligence is the most important challenge of our generation. I'm dedicating evenings and weekends to this work and investing $2,000 of personal savings. **Skills**: - Software development and Python (professional experience at Dorrance) - Research and writing - Project scoping and delivery **Team**: Priya Raman (data analyst, 5 hours/week committed) will lead categorization and analysis. We met at an AI safety meetup where I presented Halcyon Threshold. **Approach**: I'm following the \"pick one narrow thing and do it well\" principle. This is achievable in scope, addresses a real gap, and creates durable infrastructure. **Accountability**: I will be personally responsible for delivery. I'll provide monthly updates and make all work public. If this project doesn't deliver value, it will be obvious. ### Budget **Development & Research**: $8,000 - 160 hours of skilled labor (Morgan: 120 hrs, Priya: 40 hrs @ $50/hr) - Note: This is significantly below market rate ($150+/hr for this skill set) because we're mission-driven. Actual time invested will be higher. **Infrastructure**: $500 - Database hosting (PostgreSQL, $20/month × 12 = $240) - Web hosting (static site + API, $15/month × 12 = $180) - Domain renewal ($15) - SSL certificates and CDN ($65) **Research Access**: $500 - Academic paper access for comprehensive incident collection - News archive access - Industry report subscriptions **Total**: $9,000 ### Success Metrics **Concrete deliverables**: - ✅ 500+ incidents documented with standardized categorization - ✅ Public web interface launched at halcyonthreshold.org - ✅ Methodology document published - ✅ Write-up on Alignment Commons **Impact metrics** (6-month horizon): - Used by at least 5 AI safety researchers or organizations - Cited in at least 2 research papers or policy documents - 10+ community submissions per month - Positive feedback from domain experts **Failure condition**: If by month 3 we have fewer than 200 incidents or no researchers find it useful, I'll publish a retrospective on what went wrong and return unused funds. ### Risk & Mitigation **Technical risks**: - Scope too ambitious → Focus on quality over quantity, launch with 200 high-quality incidents - Categorization inconsistent → Develop clear rubrics, get expert review early - Low community adoption → Proactively reach out to researchers, make sure it solves real problems **Sustainability**: After the grant period, I'll maintain updates with 2-3 hours/week from personal time. If the project proves valuable, we'll seek additional funding for expansion. If not valuable, we'll sunset it gracefully. **If grant rejected**: I'll start with my $2,000 personal budget, build a minimal viable version, and reapply for funding later based on demonstrated value. --- Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold morgan@halcyonthreshold.org November 16, 2026"
rows.quote: Submitted grant application to Emberfall Fund ($9,000 request, due Nov 30)
